canonical_name: Whitney ear-construction theorem family for finite non-separable graphs
statement_blocker: The catalog does not choose the construction implication, converse, or biconditional and does not define 2-connectedness or an ear. Whitney's inspected Theorem 19 and following converse concern finite non-separable graphs that may have loops and parallel arcs; a modern SimpleGraph formulation must resolve the non-separable/2-vertex-connected transport, size and loop qualifications, initial circuits, single-edge versus suspended-chain ears, ordered decomposition and coverage. Selecting an expression at intake would bypass the assigned statement phase.
target_decision: preserve Whitney's source-backed ear-construction family and require independent source acceptance plus an explicit modern graph-model and connectivity transport before exact statement freeze
domain_and_universes: Open: the accepted statement must choose Whitney's finite multigraph-like arc model or a source-justified finite SimpleGraph specialization, fix the vertex universe, finiteness and decidability presentation, and define the carrier for cycles, ears, partial graphs and decomposition order.
conclusion: Open formal encoding of the construction direction, converse, or biconditional relating the selected non-separable or 2-vertex-connected predicate to a complete ordered ear construction from a cycle.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before the exact proposition is frozen; the statement phase must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md without silently adding source-external hypotheses.
candidate_scope_not_credited: every finite non-separable graph with at least two arcs can be built from a circuit by successively adding arcs or suspended chains while all partial graphs remain non-separable

a formulation through two internally vertex-disjoint paths

triangles, longer cycles, and the zero-additional-ear case

the at-least-two-arcs source premise versus the modern at-least-three-vertices convention
excluded_substitutions: ordinary connectedness or 2-edge-connectivity in place of 2-vertex-connectivity
a closed-ear, directed-ear, convex-ear, matroid-ear, or matching-covered-graph theorem
only preservation after one attached path when the selected root requires a complete construction
